searchText: I think this is fundamentally wrong unless "free" here means it requires no resources, a 10 year old can click on a Windows icon and it will sync immediately and start working flawlessly and if the user makes a mistake there will be a million barriers the software puts to prevent this (sending to a wrong address, network, paying too much gas, etc). I venture to say this will **never** happen and users will always be centralized no matter what the protocol does That is why I mentioned that "free" was a hypothetical extreme to illustrate the point. The closer we get to that hypothetical free, the better. Just because it isn't achievable in the purest sense doesn't mean there isn't value in striving for it. That I agree, but the centralization aspect I think is something we'll have to live with forever To some extent, yes. However, I think we can make huge gains with in-browser light clients. If most dapps can operate without a centrally run node that is a huge win IMO.
